A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UEC research work. All 29 pages of v2 and 36 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original MIRACL and MMTEB experiments, component ablations, embedding-alignment measurements, and additional benchmark results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds multilingual evaluations, calibration diagnostics, covariance and fitting-data analyses, and hyperparameter sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 and the coefficient derivation replace v2's normalized inverse-trace weighting and unregularized linear objective with an entropy-regularized objective and weights proportional to exp(-tr(Sigma)/T). This changes the central aggregation rule. Temperature tuning already appeared in v2's experimental details; the last-layer Laplace conversion and similarity estimator remain.

E1.justification: Appendix B.5 expands explicit language coverage to seven non-English Wikipedia retrieval languages, German/French/Italian legal classification, and twelve SemRel24STS languages, extending the corresponding selected-language results in v2. Bitext mining, clustering, and reranking were already evaluated in v2 and are retained.

E2.justification: The original benchmark comparator sets remain. v3 additionally compares KFAC with diagonal Laplace approximation in Table 17. Its new multilingual Tables 14–16 omit GroVE, and the retrieval table also omits Borda, although these comparators remain in the corresponding main-task tables.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1 and B.3.2 change the stated MIRACL sample count from 25 to 100 per language, despite unchanged reported scores; this establishes a reported protocol revision, not a verified rerun. New diagnostics introduce classification ECE evaluation, ten-quantile-bin Var-ECE, covariance/layer/subsampling controls, and temperature and variance-scaling sweeps.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, CCA analysis, alternative similarities, and challenging example, v3 adds direct uncertainty-calibration diagnostics, diagonal-versus-KFAC analysis, one-to-six-layer comparisons, fitting-data sparsity tests, and beta/temperature sensitivity on MIRACL and StackOverflow. These examine previously untested aspects of uncertainty quality and robustness.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, experimental error bars, or significance tests. The added ECE and Var-ECE evaluations measure model uncertainty quality; they do not introduce uncertainty estimates around the reported experimental results.

E6.justification: The main benchmark tables and MIRACL scores remain numerically unchanged. v3 adds extensive multilingual, calibration, robustness, and sensitivity results, including UEC ECE of 0.032 and Var-ECE of 0.028. The similarity-comparison table revises relative KLD runtime from 1.48 to 1.52 and 2-Wasserstein runtime from 1.60 to 2.37; these are revised reports, not established same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: v3 replaces the invalid derivation of inverse weights from a linear simplex objective with an entropy-regularized convex derivation yielding softmax coefficients. It also defines Var-ECE mathematically and revises diagonal-covariance complexity accounting. The expanded Laplace exposition largely restates existing mathematics, while the Wasserstein and Jeffreys arguments are substantially retained and renumbered.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and contribution list remove v2's central Bayes-optimal weighting claim and instead describe coefficients derived from a principled surrogate formulation. The conclusion newly claims the first fully post-hoc, uncertainty-calibrated embedding ensemble. These revise the claimed theoretical guarantee and novelty while retaining the overall framework and performance claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds an entropy-as-prior interpretation, explanations favoring diagonal and last-layer Laplace approximations, calibration and sparsity interpretations, and an explicit limitation to epistemic uncertainty. Appendix B.2 acknowledges linear complexity for competing diagonal-covariance distances. New multilingual interpretations assert no language-wise degradation, although Tables 14–15 contain exceptions.

D1.justification: The added diagnostics disclose covariance alternatives, layer counts, fitting-data fractions, and ten-bin variance-calibration construction. Appendix D identifies favorable hyperparameter regions. Existing fitting datasets and sample counts, main temperature settings, beta search range, and code/library access statements are retained; the PDFs do not disclose new hardware or repeated-run information.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations supporting Laplace approximations, entropy regularization, and retrieval constraints, including Hobbhahn, Sharma, Sagawa, Nguyen, Zhao, Zhdanov, and Zhou. The related-work discussion remains largely unchanged, with a limited novelty refinement in the conclusion. Consolidating duplicate Khan references and updating Matryoshka bibliographic details do not introduce different prior work.

P1.justification: Rewriting concentrates on the Laplace and coefficient explanations, coefficient derivation, and conclusion. Detailed Laplace exposition is organized into Appendix A.1, diagnostic sections are inserted, and publication headers and acknowledgements are updated. The overall narrative structure and much of the introduction, related work, existing experiments, and remaining proofs are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds eight tables presenting calibration, multilingual comparisons, and Laplace robustness, plus two two-panel sensitivity figures. These substantially expand the visual evidence. Existing figures and tables are mostly retained, with some formula/caption refinements, resizing, relocation, and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The corrected coefficient derivation and direct calibration and sensitivity diagnostics improve the foundation and evaluation of the uncertainty claims. However, experimental reporting limits the overall gain: MIRACL's stated sample count changes while its scores remain identical, and new multilingual interpretations overstate the evidence. For example, Appendix B.5 claims no degradation against the strongest individual model, but Table 14 reports Persian nDCG@10 of 16.92 for UEC versus 35.69 for GTE-MB. The revision provides useful improvements without establishing a clear substantial overall quality gain.
